title: Loss Mitigation Basis for Home Mortgage Loans: Establishing a Forbearance Plan and Its Month Limits
content:
Forbearance on a Home Mortgage Loans note is the borrower's own signed agreement. The agent's part is to register a forbearance request naming the hardship type; the plan itself starts only after the borrower signs.

**The hardship.** The hardship must be one of the hardship types the loan's program treats as eligible. The hardship type is what the borrower states on the request, and it is that statement, correlated to the request, that the eligibility is read against.

**The length of a first plan.** A first plan lasts no more than the program's longest first plan, in months.

**The total over the life of the loan.** The months of all plans on the loan, including the one being established, may not exceed the program's longest total forbearance. The months already used are taken from the bank's record of that loan, and not from the borrower's account of them.

## The conditions and where each is decided

| Condition | Decided from |
|---|---|
| The hardship type is eligible on the program | What the borrower states on the request |
| A first plan is within the program's longest first plan | The months of the plan being established |
| All plans together are within the program's longest total | The months already used on the loan, in the bank's records, together with the months of this plan |
| The plan has started | The borrower having signed |

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Take a loan on a program whose longest first plan is 3 months and whose longest total forbearance is 12 months.

- As a first plan, one of 3 months is within the program's longest first plan; one of 4 months is not.
- Where the loan's records show 9 months of plans already used, a further plan of 3 months brings the months of all plans, including this one, to 12, which does not exceed the program's longest total. A further plan of 4 months would bring them to 13, which does.
